lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Education appears before the stronger work history.
items.because: For an established finance candidate, starting with Education delays the experience most likely to interest a recruiter.

items.says: The Lakeside entry takes attention from the finance direction without explaining its relevance to the current transition.
items.because: It is the most recent role but is less connected to the finance work elsewhere.

items.says: The older Student Investment Fund entry is longer than its relevance warrants.
items.because: Giving student-era tasks equal weight can dilute more recent, stronger accomplishments.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund entry does not prioritize its clearest fund-specific accomplishment.
items.because: The benchmark-reporting result is more clearly tied to the fund than the other tasks.

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They draw attention to personal characteristics rather than qualifications.

items.says: The caddie duties do not show a benefit to the members or club.
“About 5 rounds a week” is informal and imprecise.
The tournament support has no stated result.
The line does not name the tournament task handled.
The line gives no indication of the tournament’s size.
The 40% close-efficiency improvement has no comparison or baseline.
The template’s standardization is described at length without stating its business effect.
The board-pack commentary does not say what it affected.
The variance threshold makes “each line” sound like every line in the pack.
Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC mismatches the cash flow and discount rate.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity should be discounted at the cost of equity; WACC is generally used for free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The acquisition valuation has no stated result or consequence.
Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: A group margin is total EBITDA divided by total revenue, or a revenue-weighted average of unit margins.

items.says: The reported margin is not connected to a decision or action.
The 45% margin has no reporting period.
The forecast’s strongest results are buried after the work description.
items.because: A scanning reader may stop before reaching the low error and early debt repayment.

items.says: The underwriting bullet does not indicate how credit risk was assessed.
The approval increase and unchanged early defaults are buried after the opening description.
items.because: A scanning reader may not reach those results.

items.says: “My findings” breaks the résumé’s phrasing style.
The line does not say what analysis led to the threshold changes.
“Writes” is present tense even though the role ended in December 2022.
items.because: It conflicts with the role dates and implies the responsibility is ongoing.

items.says: The checklist does not describe the monitoring control it introduced.
The spreading template does not identify the feature that made it effective.
The sensitivity statement does not say whether the discount rate increased or decreased.
“Which used it” leaves unclear whether the club used the model or the note.
The FP&A bullet does not name a specific task.
The FP&A bullet gives no outcome from the work.
The committee’s repeated use of the report is buried in the trailing clause.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the clearest evidence that the report was useful.

items.says: The benchmark comparison does not say what it revealed.
The line does not identify what changed in the rebuilt performance report.
The cash-forecast achievement appears under both the Student Investment Fund and Stonebridge roles.
items.because: The same forecast figures are assigned to roles several years apart, leaving unclear which role produced the result.

items.says: The line does not explain how the cash forecast was built.
items.because: A reader cannot see what forecasting approach or analysis was applied.

items.says: The forecast-error figure is not defined.
items.because: Without a measure or comparison basis, the figure is harder to assess.

items.says: “About 4%” is imprecise wording for the forecast error.
items.because: It sounds like an estimate without explaining its basis.
